uninstaller.title: Uninstaller
uninstaller.subtitle: Remove programs and Store apps, then clean the files and registry entries they leave behind
uninstaller.showRuntimesHint: Runtimes such as Visual C++, .NET, and WebView2 are used by other programs and are hidden by default.

badgeHints.admin: Installed for all users — removing it and its leftovers usually needs administrator rights.
badgeHints.quiet: Supports quick uninstall without the vendor's prompts.

uninstaller.storeUnavailable: Store apps could not be listed on this system. Desktop programs are complete.

confirm.body: Each program's own uninstaller runs one at a time. Afterwards PC Toolkit Pro scans for leftovers and lets you review them before anything is deleted.
confirm.quietHint: Skip the vendor's prompts when the installer supports it (MSI, Inno Setup, NSIS, Squirrel, or a vendor quiet command). Others run normally.
confirm.scanLeftoversHint: Find remaining folders, registry entries, shortcuts, startup entries, services, scheduled tasks, and firewall rules.
confirm.restorePointHint: Lets you roll Windows back if something goes wrong. Windows creates at most one restore point per day.
confirm.restorePointNeedsAdmin: Requires running PC Toolkit Pro as administrator.
confirm.forceBody: Force remove skips the program's uninstaller and scans for everything it owns, including its folder and uninstall entry. Review the results before deleting.
confirm.adminHint: Some selected programs are installed for all users. Without administrator rights their leftovers in Program Files, ProgramData, and machine-wide registry keys are skipped. Restart as administrator first for a complete cleanup.

leftovers.title: Leftovers found
leftovers.reviewHint: Matched by name only. Check that it belongs to the removed program before deleting.
leftovers.adminHint: Needs administrator rights. Skipped when PC Toolkit Pro is not elevated.
leftovers.adminNotice: Some selected items need administrator rights and will be skipped.
leftovers.confirmTitle: Delete {count} leftover item? | Delete {count} leftover items?
leftovers.confirmBody: Files and folders are moved to the Recycle Bin. Registry entries are exported to a .reg backup in the PC Toolkit Pro data folder before they are deleted.

dialog.autoContinue: PC Toolkit Pro continues automatically when the uninstaller finishes, then scans for leftovers.
dialog.found: {count} leftover item found | {count} leftover items found

listing.hint: Listing only reads program information; nothing is changed.

deepCleaner.recycleBinDetail: Empty the Recycle Bin as Explorer shows it for your account.
deepCleaner.diskCleanupDetail: Launch Windows Disk Cleanup. Windows may ask for elevation.
deepCleaner.freeMemoryDetail: Optimize selected memory areas using the Memory Cleaner engine and report measured free RAM change.
deepCleaner.scanHint: Scanning only reads file information; cancelling changes nothing
deepCleaner.cleanHint: Cancel stops as soon as the current step allows. Already deleted files stay deleted.
deepCleaner.findBody: Scan system, app, browser, and developer caches. Review everything before you clean.
deepCleaner.summaryCount: Found {count} cleanable item | Found {count} cleanable items

confirm.title: Confirm cleanup
confirm.closeAppsHint: Save your work first. Selected apps close before cleanup; items still in use are skipped
confirm.forceTitle: Some apps did not close normally

confirm.limitedNote: Very large — estimate is a lower bound

rules.recycleBinDetail: Empty the Recycle Bin as Explorer shows it for your account.
rules.thumbnailCacheDetail: Windows regenerates previews and icons as folders are opened again.
rules.internetTempDetail: Saved passwords and browsing history are kept. Some pages may load again.
rules.userTempDetail: Files in your Windows TEMP folders. Locked files are skipped.
rules.directxShaderCacheDetail: NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel shader caches plus Windows D3DSCache. Games may briefly recompile shaders.
rules.errorReportsDetail: Windows continues to work, but removed reports are no longer available for troubleshooting.
rules.deliveryOptimizationDetail: Update files Windows shares with other PCs, removed through Windows Disk Cleanup.
rules.windowsUpdateCleanupDetail: Downloaded Windows Update packages under SoftwareDistribution. Cleaning usually needs administrator. Windows may re-download updates.
rules.previousInstallationsDetail: Windows.old from a major upgrade. Often 10 GB or more. Cleaning requires administrator; declining leaves files untouched.
rules.stalePartialDownloadsDetail: Incomplete browser downloads in Downloads older than 7 days. Finished files and recent transfers are kept.
rules.whatsappCacheDetail: WebView cache under WhatsApp packages. Accounts, messages, and settings are kept. Close WhatsApp before cleaning.
rules.telegramTempDetail: Telegram temp and dump folders. Accounts, chats, downloaded media, and settings are kept.
rules.discordCacheDetail: Discord GPU, code, Dawn, and log caches. Close Discord before cleaning for best results.
rules.steamCacheDetail: Steam htmlcache browser caches. Installed games and screenshots are kept. Close Steam first.
rules.teamsCacheDetail: Teams WebView caches. Chats, files, and account data are kept. Close Teams first.
rules.spotifyCacheDetail: Spotify Browser and Storage cache folders. Playlists, downloads, and login are kept.
rules.slackCacheDetail: Slack GPU, code, and HTTP caches. Workspaces and messages are kept. Close Slack first.
rules.notionCacheDetail: Notion GPU, code, and HTTP caches. Pages and account data are kept. Close Notion first.
rules.dockerDesktopCacheDetail: Docker Desktop Electron/UI caches only — not images, volumes, or build cache. Close Docker Desktop first.
rules.chromeCacheDetail: Passwords, cookies, history, extensions, and bookmarks are kept. Close the browser first.
rules.chromeOfflineCacheDetail: Passwords, history, and bookmarks are kept. Some sites may download offline content again.
rules.edgeCacheDetail: Passwords, cookies, history, extensions, and bookmarks are kept. Close the browser first.
rules.edgeOfflineCacheDetail: Passwords, history, and bookmarks are kept. Some sites may download offline content again.
rules.braveCacheDetail: Passwords, cookies, history, extensions, and bookmarks are kept. Close the browser first.
rules.vivaldiCacheDetail: Passwords, cookies, history, extensions, and bookmarks are kept. Close the browser first.
rules.chromiumCacheDetail: Passwords, cookies, history, extensions, and bookmarks are kept. Close the browser first.
rules.operaCacheDetail: Opera and Opera GX caches. Passwords, history, and bookmarks are kept. Close the browser first.
rules.firefoxCacheDetail: Firefox cache2, startup, and shader caches across profiles. Bookmarks and logins are kept.
rules.npmCacheDetail: npm package download cache. Packages may be downloaded again.
rules.pnpmStoreDetail: pnpm content-addressable store cache. Packages may be fetched again.
rules.pipCacheDetail: Python pip wheel and HTTP cache.
rules.uvCacheDetail: Projects, virtual environments, and managed Python installs are kept. Packages may download again.
rules.cargoCacheDetail: Rust Cargo registry, git checkouts, and rustup downloads. Crates may be fetched again.
rules.goBuildCacheDetail: Go compiler build cache. Modules are kept; the next build may recompile.
rules.nugetCacheDetail: NuGet v3 HTTP cache, plugins-cache, scratch, and global packages folder.
rules.gradleCachesDetail: Gradle caches, daemon, workers, and notifications under .gradle.
rules.mavenRepositoryDetail: Local Maven .m2/repository artifacts. Builds may download packages again.
rules.jetbrainsCachesDetail: JetBrains and Android Studio caches, indexes, logs, and compile-server folders. Indexes may rebuild.
rules.vsCacheDetail: Visual Studio component, MEF, and image caches. Settings, extensions, and installer packages are kept.
rules.nodeToolingDetail: node-gyp, Corepack, Electron, and electron-builder download caches.
rules.playwrightCacheDetail: Playwright, Cypress, Puppeteer, and Selenium browser and driver downloads. They can be re-downloaded.
rules.androidCacheDetail: Android SDK temp/cache and user .android build caches. SDKs and AVDs are kept.
rules.editorCacheDetail: VS Code, Cursor, VSCodium, and Windsurf Cache/CachedData/GPUCache/logs. Settings and extensions stay.
rules.systemErrorReportsDetail: Machine-wide Windows Error Reporting queue and archive. Cleaning needs administrator.
rules.windowsLogsDetail: Setup, servicing, and diagnostic logs older than 3 days in the Windows Logs, Panther, and LogFiles folders. Needs administrator; logs are no longer available for troubleshooting.
rules.arcCacheDetail: Passwords, cookies, history, extensions, and bookmarks are kept. Close the browser first.
rules.duckduckgoCacheDetail: WebView2 caches of the DuckDuckGo browser. Bookmarks, passwords, and history are kept. Close the browser first.
rules.floorpCacheDetail: Floorp cache2, startup, and shader caches across profiles. Bookmarks and logins are kept.
rules.librewolfCacheDetail: LibreWolf cache2, startup, and shader caches across profiles. Bookmarks and logins are kept.
rules.waterfoxCacheDetail: Waterfox cache2, startup, and shader caches across profiles. Bookmarks and logins are kept.
rules.thunderbirdCacheDetail: Thunderbird web-content, startup, and shader caches. Mail, accounts, and address books are kept.
rules.figmaCacheDetail: Figma desktop GPU, code, and HTTP caches plus logs. Files and sign-in are kept. Close Figma first.
rules.obsidianCacheDetail: Obsidian app GPU, code, and HTTP caches. Vaults, plugins, and settings are kept. Close Obsidian first.
rules.insomniaCacheDetail: Insomnia GPU, code, and HTTP caches plus logs. Collections and environments are kept. Close Insomnia first.
rules.githubDesktopCacheDetail: GitHub Desktop GPU, code, and HTTP caches plus logs. Repositories and sign-in are kept. Close GitHub Desktop first.
rules.postmanCacheDetail: Postman GPU, code, and HTTP caches plus logs. Collections, workspaces, and sign-in are kept. Close Postman first.
rules.signalCacheDetail: Signal desktop GPU, code, and HTTP caches plus logs. Messages, attachments, and the account are kept. Close Signal first.
rules.dropboxCacheDetail: Dropbox desktop rendering caches only. Synced files are never touched. Close Dropbox first.
rules.claudeCacheDetail: Claude desktop GPU, code, and HTTP caches plus logs. Chats, settings, and sign-in are kept. Close the Claude app first.
rules.codexCacheDetail: Codex desktop browser caches and logs. Sessions, settings, and sign-in are kept. Close the Codex app first.
rules.battleNetCacheDetail: Battle.net launcher and browser caches. Installed games and sign-in are kept. Close Battle.net first.
rules.eaDesktopCacheDetail: EA app browser caches. Installed games and sign-in are kept. Close the EA app first.
rules.epicLauncherCacheDetail: Epic Games Launcher web caches, logs, and crash reports. Installed games and sign-in are kept. Close the launcher first.
rules.adobeMediaCacheDetail: Premiere Pro, After Effects, and Media Encoder media cache files. They are rebuilt on next import, which can take time for large projects.
rules.zoomLogsDetail: Zoom log files older than 14 days. Meetings, recordings, and settings are kept.
rules.obsLogsDetail: OBS Studio logs and crash reports older than 14 days. Scenes, profiles, and recordings are kept.
rules.vlcCacheDetail: Downloaded album art and crash dumps. Playlists, media library, and preferences are kept.
rules.electronUpdaterCacheDetail: Pending update packages and cached installers in app updater folders. Apps download them again on their next update check.
rules.bunCacheDetail: Bun package download cache. Packages may be downloaded again.
rules.denoCacheDetail: Deno remote module, npm, and compile caches. Installed scripts are kept; modules may download again.
rules.composerCacheDetail: PHP Composer package and metadata cache. Composer settings and credentials are kept.
rules.vcpkgArchivesDetail: vcpkg prebuilt package archives. Libraries may be rebuilt from source, which can take a long time.
rules.sccacheCacheDetail: Shared compilation cache for Rust and C/C++. The next build may be slower.
rules.ccacheCacheDetail: C/C++ compiler cache. ccache.conf is kept; the next build may be slower.
rules.terraformPluginCacheDetail: Shared Terraform provider plugin cache. Providers may download again on init.
rules.poetryCacheDetail: Poetry package artifacts and metadata cache. Poetry virtual environments are kept.
rules.pyenvCacheDetail: Downloaded Python installers. Installed Python versions are kept.
rules.pythonToolCachesDetail: Global Ruff and mypy caches. Results are recomputed on the next run.
rules.preCommitCacheDetail: pre-commit hook environments. They are rebuilt on the next commit, which may take a while.
rules.hexCacheDetail: Elixir Hex package cache. Packages may download again.
rules.sbtIvyCacheDetail: sbt boot/preloaded folders and the Ivy cache. Dependencies may download again.
rules.dartServerCacheDetail: Dart and Flutter analysis server cache. Indexes rebuild when the editor opens a project.
rules.copilotCliLeftoversDetail: Interrupted GitHub Copilot CLI package extractions. The installed CLI is kept.
rules.huggingfaceXetCacheDetail: Xet chunk and shard caches and logs. Downloaded models and in-progress transfers are kept; data may download again.

special.temporarySetupFilesDetail: Files left behind by Windows and app installers, removed through Windows Disk Cleanup. Requires administrator.
special.updateCleanupDetail: Superseded update components kept by Windows servicing, removed through Windows Disk Cleanup. Installed updates can no longer be uninstalled afterwards. Requires administrator.
special.dockerBuildCacheDetail: Unused build cache on the default Docker context, pruned with Docker's own command. Images and containers are kept; the next build may take longer.
special.condaCleanDetail: Downloaded package archives, index cache, and logs, removed with conda clean. Environments are kept.
special.rustToolchainsDetail: rustup toolchains that are not the default, active, overridden, or pinned by a project on this PC. Removed with rustup; reinstall with rustup when needed.

startup.withWindowsBody: Open PC Toolkit Pro when you sign in, so auto RAM cleanup and your other settings keep working after a restart.
startup.minimizedBody: When Windows starts it, stay in the tray instead of opening the window. Opening it yourself always shows the window.
startup.runAsAdminBody: Full cleaning everywhere (all memory areas, admin-only fixes). Opening it shows the normal Windows prompt; with Start with Windows, a sign-in task starts it as administrator without asking each time.
startup.noteElevatedTask: Starts as administrator at sign-in through a Windows scheduled task.
startup.noteNeedsAdminCreate: Restart as administrator once to finish setup. Until then Windows asks for permission at sign-in.
startup.noteNeedsAdminRemove: Restart as administrator once to remove the old administrator sign-in task.
startup.noteFailed: Windows did not accept the startup change. Try again, or restart as administrator.

engine.subtitle: One scan for junk, privacy traces, startup, security, and disk health

home.scanHint: Read-only. Nothing changes until you review and fix.
home.noneSelected: Pick at least one category to scan.
home.autoFix: Auto fix safe items after the scan
home.autoFixHint: Only items marked Safe are fixed automatically. Items that need review are never auto-fixed.

scanning.stopMessage: Categories that have not finished will be marked as skipped.

results.noItems: Nothing to show for this category.

badges.adminHint: Needs PC Toolkit Pro running as administrator; skipped otherwise.

summary.undoHint: {count} change can be undone. | {count} changes can be undone.
summary.afterActionFailed: The after-fix power action could not run.
summary.undoDone: {restored} restored, {skipped} skipped (changed since the fix or needs admin).

afterAction.restart: Restarting in {seconds} s — save your work.

reasons.itemsFailed: Some files could not be removed

details.adminOk: Needed — this copy runs as administrator, so it can be fixed.
details.adminNeeded: Needed — restart PC Toolkit Pro as administrator to fix this item.
details.notFixable: Nothing is changed from here. Use the button to open the Windows page that handles it.

values.unreadable: Cannot be read without administrator rights
values.removePolicy: Remove the policy value so Windows’ own setting applies
values.yes: Yes — close it first or the item is skipped
values.browserOpen: {browser} is open right now. Close it first, otherwise this item is skipped.

riskMeaning.safe: Safe — rebuildable or reversible; selected automatically and included in Auto fix.
riskMeaning.review: Review — you might want to keep it; never selected or auto-fixed unless you tick it.

fix.generic: Applies the fix for this item and checks it again first; anything that changed since the scan is skipped.
fix.privacy: Deletes these traces. Registry lists are exported to a .reg backup first; browser files are only removed while the browser is closed. Deleted files cannot be restored.
fix.junk: Deletes these cache files permanently with Deep Cleanup’s safety checks; apps rebuild them when needed. Files in use are skipped.
fix.shortcuts: Moves the broken shortcut to the Recycle Bin, so you can restore it.
fix.registry: Exports the key to a .reg backup, then deletes it. Double-click the backup to restore it; it is also listed in Undo.
fix.startup: Stops it from starting with Windows the same way Task Manager does — the program is not removed and you can turn it back on in the Startup tab. Broken entries are deleted after a backup.
fix.security: Writes the recommended value after saving the current one. Use Undo to restore the previous value.
fix.protection: Turns the firewall profile back on through Windows Firewall. Undo restores the previous state.
fix.software: Updates the app with winget (Microsoft’s package manager) using the publisher’s installer.
fix.diskHealth: Runs Windows’ online disk check; repairs that need a restart are only scheduled.
fix.diskOptimize: Runs Windows’ own drive optimizer (TRIM for SSDs, defragmentation for hard drives).

hint.smart: Smart recommendation selects only safe items: rebuildable caches, broken shortcuts and settings that can be undone. History, cookies, startup apps, registry entries and updates are left for you to decide.
hint.all: Everything fixable is selected, including Review items such as browser history, cookies and startup apps — check the list before fixing.
hint.none: Nothing is selected. Tick the items you want to fix.

privacy.recentItemsDetail: Shortcuts to recently opened files in the Recent folder. The files themselves are not touched.
privacy.jumpListsDetail: Recent and pinned entries shown when you right-click apps on the taskbar or Start. Pinned jump-list entries are removed too.

mru.recentDocsDetail: Explorer's list of recently opened documents. A .reg backup is saved before it is cleared.
mru.runMruDetail: Commands typed in the Run dialog (Win+R). A .reg backup is saved before it is cleared.
mru.typedPathsDetail: Paths typed in the File Explorer address bar. A .reg backup is saved before it is cleared.
mru.searchHistoryDetail: Searches typed in the File Explorer search box. A .reg backup is saved before it is cleared.
mru.openSaveMruDetail: Files recently chosen in Open and Save dialogs. A .reg backup is saved before it is cleared.
mru.lastVisitedMruDetail: Folders recently used by apps in Open and Save dialogs. A .reg backup is saved before it is cleared.

browser.historyDetail: Websites you visited and your download list in this profile. Bookmarks, passwords and open tabs are kept.
browser.cookiesDetail: Logins to websites in this profile — you will be signed out of sites. Saved passwords and bookmarks are kept.
browser.formDataDetail: Text the browser remembers for web forms in this profile. Saved passwords are kept.

junk.description: System, app, and browser caches recommended by Deep Cleanup. Never the Recycle Bin or Downloads.

missingTarget.desktop: Desktop shortcut whose target no longer exists. It is moved to the Recycle Bin.
missingTarget.startMenu: Start menu shortcut whose target no longer exists. It is moved to the Recycle Bin.

orphanUninstall.detail: The program's uninstaller and install folder no longer exist, so this entry in Installed apps cannot do anything. A .reg backup is saved before it is removed.

orphanAppPath.title: Broken app shortcut registration: {name}
orphanAppPath.detail: Windows has a Run-dialog registration for this program, but its executable no longer exists. A .reg backup is saved before it is removed.

orphanSharedDll.title: Stale shared file counter: {name}
orphanSharedDll.detail: A shared-file reference count points to a file that no longer exists. Removing it is tidy-up only and does not speed up Windows. The previous value is kept for undo.

uacEnabled.title: User Account Control is turned off
uacEnabled.detail: Every program runs with full administrator rights. Turning UAC back on takes effect after a restart.

uacSecureDesktop.title: UAC prompts do not use the secure desktop
uacSecureDesktop.detail: Other programs could imitate or click elevation prompts. The secure desktop isolates them.

uacAdminPrompt.title: Administrators are elevated without a prompt
uacAdminPrompt.detail: Programs can gain administrator rights silently. Restores the Windows default (prompt for consent for non-Windows programs).

remoteUacFiltering.title: Remote UAC restrictions are disabled
remoteUacFiltering.detail: Local administrator accounts get full rights over the network, which helps attackers move between PCs. Removes the override so the Windows default applies.

smartScreenApps.title: SmartScreen for apps and files is off
smartScreenApps.detail: Windows does not warn before running unrecognized downloaded programs. Sets it back to warn.

smartScreenPolicy.title: A policy turns SmartScreen off
smartScreenPolicy.detail: A local policy disables SmartScreen for the whole PC. Removing the policy returns control to Windows Security. Organization-managed PCs may set it again.

smartScreenStoreApps.title: SmartScreen for Microsoft Store apps is off
smartScreenStoreApps.detail: Web content used by Store apps is not checked for malicious sites.

autorunAllDrives.title: AutoRun is allowed on some drive types
autorunAllDrives.detail: Drives such as CDs can start programs automatically when inserted. Disables AutoRun on all drive types.

autorunInf.title: autorun.inf files are processed
autorunInf.detail: Windows still reads autorun.inf commands from media. Disabling it blocks a common malware spreading trick.

autoplay.title: AutoPlay is on
autoplay.detail: Windows offers actions automatically when media or devices are connected. Turning it off is optional — you can still open drives manually.

smb1Server.title: SMB 1.0 file sharing server is enabled
smb1Server.detail: SMB 1.0 is obsolete and was used by WannaCry-style attacks. Disables the server side; takes effect after a restart.

restrictAnonymousSam.title: Anonymous users can list accounts
restrictAnonymousSam.detail: Anyone on the network could enumerate the PC's user accounts without signing in.

restrictAnonymous.title: Anonymous users can list shares
restrictAnonymous.detail: Anyone on the network could enumerate shared folders without signing in. Very old network devices may rely on this — review before changing.

everyoneIncludesAnonymous.title: Anonymous users are treated as Everyone
everyoneIncludesAnonymous.detail: Permissions granted to Everyone would also apply to unauthenticated users.

noLmHash.title: Weak LAN Manager password hashes are stored
noLmHash.detail: LM hashes can be cracked in seconds. Stops storing them at the next password change.

lmCompatibility.title: Weak network authentication (LM / NTLMv1) is allowed
lmCompatibility.detail: The PC may send easily cracked responses when signing in to network resources. Restores the Windows default (NTLMv2 only).

limitBlankPasswords.title: Accounts with blank passwords can sign in over the network
limitBlankPasswords.detail: Accounts without a password should only be usable at the PC itself.

wdigestCredentials.title: Sign-in passwords are kept in memory in plain text
wdigestCredentials.detail: WDigest stores reusable passwords that credential-stealing tools can read.

lsaProtection.title: LSA protection is off
lsaProtection.detail: Runs the Windows sign-in service as a protected process so tools cannot read credentials from it. Some older security or smart-card drivers are incompatible — review before enabling. Takes effect after a restart.

llmnr.title: Multicast name resolution (LLMNR) is enabled
llmnr.detail: LLMNR can be spoofed on local networks to capture credentials. Some home networks use it to find devices by name — review before changing.

sehop.title: Exception chain validation (SEHOP) is off
sehop.detail: SEHOP blocks a common class of exploits. Restores the Windows default.

windowsScriptHost.title: Windows Script Host is enabled
windowsScriptHost.detail: Malicious .vbs and .js email attachments run through Windows Script Host. Some installers and logon scripts need it — review before disabling.

alwaysInstallElevatedMachine.title: Installers always run with administrator rights
alwaysInstallElevatedMachine.detail: Any user can install a package that runs with full system rights. Removes the policy.

alwaysInstallElevatedUser.title: Installers always run with administrator rights for this user
alwaysInstallElevatedUser.detail: Combined with the machine policy, any package runs with full system rights. Removes the policy.

pointAndPrint.title: Printer drivers install without elevation
pointAndPrint.detail: Point and Print can install untrusted printer drivers without a prompt (PrintNightmare). Removes the override.

remoteDesktop.title: Remote Desktop is enabled
remoteDesktop.detail: The PC accepts Remote Desktop connections. Turn it off only if you do not connect to this PC remotely.

remoteDesktopNla.title: Remote Desktop does not require Network Level Authentication
remoteDesktopNla.detail: Connections can reach the sign-in screen before authenticating, which exposes the PC to attacks.

remoteAssistance.title: Remote Assistance is allowed
remoteAssistance.detail: Others can be invited to control this PC. Turn it off if you do not use Remote Assistance.

autoLogonPassword.title: Automatic sign-in stores a password in plain text
autoLogonPassword.detail: Windows signs in automatically using a password saved unencrypted in the registry. Turn off automatic sign-in in the account settings if you do not need it.

secureBoot.title: Secure Boot is off
secureBoot.detail: Secure Boot blocks boot-level malware. It can only be turned on in the PC's UEFI firmware settings.

defenderPua.title: Potentially unwanted app blocking is off
defenderPua.detail: Microsoft Defender does not block adware and bundled junk software. This is set through a local policy, so Windows Security will show it as managed.

controlledFolderAccess.title: Controlled folder access is off
controlledFolderAccess.detail: Ransomware protection for your documents is off. It can block some legitimate apps, so turn it on in Windows Security if you want it.

advertisingId.title: Apps can use your advertising ID
advertisingId.detail: Apps can track you across apps to show personalized ads.

tailoredExperiences.title: Tailored experiences with diagnostic data are on
tailoredExperiences.detail: Microsoft uses your diagnostic data for personalized tips, ads, and recommendations.

suggestedContent.title: Suggested content in Settings is on
suggestedContent.detail: Windows shows promotional suggestions in the Settings app.

languageListAccess.title: Websites can read your language list
languageListAccess.detail: Websites get your installed languages, which helps fingerprint the browser.

inkingTypingPersonalization.title: Inking and typing data is sent to Microsoft
inkingTypingPersonalization.detail: Typing and handwriting data is sent to improve recognition and suggestions.

appLaunchTracking.title: Windows tracks app launches
appLaunchTracking.detail: Used to improve Start and search results. Turning it off removes the most-used list from Start — review before changing.

telemetryLevel.title: Optional diagnostic data is sent
telemetryLevel.detail: Windows sends optional diagnostic data (websites, app usage) to Microsoft. Limits it to required diagnostic data.

showFileExtensions.title: File name extensions are hidden
showFileExtensions.detail: Malicious files can disguise themselves, for example invoice.pdf.exe shown as invoice.pdf.

noAntivirus.title: No antivirus is registered
noAntivirus.detail: Windows Security does not report any antivirus. Open Windows Security to turn on Microsoft Defender Antivirus or check your security product.

antivirusOff.title: {name} is turned off
antivirusOff.detail: Real-time protection is off or snoozed. Turn it back on in Windows Security or in the antivirus program itself.

antivirusExpired.title: {name} subscription has expired
antivirusExpired.detail: This antivirus no longer protects the PC. Renew it, or remove it so Microsoft Defender Antivirus can take over.

antivirusOutdated.title: {name} protection updates are out of date
antivirusOutdated.detail: Security intelligence is outdated, so recent threats may not be detected. Check for protection updates in Windows Security.

securityCenterUnavailable.title: Windows Security status is unavailable
securityCenterUnavailable.detail: Windows Security Center did not answer, so antivirus status could not be checked on this PC.

firewallUnavailable.title: Windows Firewall status is unavailable
firewallUnavailable.detail: The firewall could not be read. The Windows Defender Firewall service may be stopped. Open Windows Security to check.

domain.title: Firewall is off for domain networks
domain.detail: Windows Defender Firewall is disabled for workplace (domain) networks. Turning it on needs administrator rights and can be undone.

private.title: Firewall is off for private networks
private.detail: Windows Defender Firewall is disabled for home and other private networks. Turning it on needs administrator rights and can be undone.

public.title: Firewall is off for public networks
public.detail: Windows Defender Firewall is disabled on public networks such as cafés and airports. Turning it on needs administrator rights and can be undone.

serviceDisabled.title: Windows Update service is disabled
serviceDisabled.detail: Windows cannot download security updates while the Windows Update service is disabled.

rebootPending.title: Restart to finish installing updates
rebootPending.detail: Updates are installed but only take effect after a restart.

checkStale.title: No successful update check for {days} days
checkStale.detail: Windows normally checks for updates every day. Open Windows Update and select Check for updates.

neverChecked.title: Windows Update has no successful check on record
neverChecked.detail: Open Windows Update and select Check for updates.

installStale.title: No updates installed for {days} days
installStale.detail: Windows releases security updates every month. Open Windows Update to see if updates are waiting or failing.

updatesPending.title: {count} update waiting to be installed | {count} updates waiting to be installed
updatesPending.detail: As of Windows Update's last check, {count} update is not installed yet ({security} with a security rating). Install it from Windows Update. | As of Windows Update's last check, {count} updates are not installed yet ({security} with a security rating). Install them from Windows Update.

checkSlow.title: The update list took too long to read
checkSlow.detail: Windows Update did not answer in time, so waiting updates could not be counted. Open Windows Update to check.

checkFailed.title: Waiting updates could not be counted
checkFailed.detail: Windows Update did not return a list of updates. Open Windows Update to check.

software.updateIdTruncated: {current} → {available}. winget shortened this package id, so it cannot be updated from here; update it in the app or with winget.

diskHealth.volumeDirtyDetail: Windows marked this drive as possibly having file system errors. Fix runs an online check (chkdsk /scan) and schedules a check at restart if a repair needs the drive offline. Requires administrator.
diskHealth.lowSpaceDetail: Only {percent}% free. Low free space slows Windows and blocks updates.
diskHealth.diskWarningDetail: Windows reports a warning for this disk ({drives}). Back up important files. Status: {status}
diskHealth.diskUnhealthyDetail: Windows reports this disk ({drives}) as unhealthy. Back up your files now and plan to replace it. Status: {status}

diskOptimize.retrimDueDetail: Runs Windows Optimize Drives (ReTrim) on this SSD. Requires administrator.
diskOptimize.defragDueDetail: Runs Windows Optimize Drives (defragment) on this hard disk. It can take a long time. Requires administrator.
diskOptimize.trimDisabledDetail: SSDs need TRIM to stay fast. Fix turns it back on (the Windows default). Requires administrator.
diskOptimize.scheduleDisabledDetail: Windows normally optimizes drives weekly (ReTrim on SSDs). Fix turns the built-in schedule back on. Requires administrator.
diskOptimize.scheduleMissingDetail: The built-in Windows optimization task was removed. Run Optimize Drives manually from time to time.

codes.invalidInput: The request was not valid. Refresh the page and try again.
codes.operationBusy: Another operation is still running. Wait for it to finish, then try again.
codes.operationFailed: The operation could not be completed. Try again.
codes.permissionDenied: Windows denied access. Restart as administrator if this keeps happening.
codes.taskJoinFailed: A background task stopped unexpectedly. Try again.
codes.notFound: The item could not be found. It may have been removed already.
codes.unknown: An unexpected error occurred. Try again.
